title: Show whether the Claude prompt cache is warm, and for how long
notes:
The user wants a cache status like the one in their screenshot: a 'WARM 42m left' pill (and 'COLD' once it has expired) beside the usage meters.

What it means: Anthropic's prompt cache lives for a fixed time after its last use, 5 minutes or 1 hour depending on how it was written; each request that reads it starts the clock again. A warm cache makes the next prompt cheap and fast; a cold one re-sends the whole context at full price.

How to know it, without new calls: every assistant message's usage carries cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens and ephemeral_1h_input_tokens, and cache_read_input_tokens. The tier is the one the session last wrote (1h if ephemeral_1h_input_tokens > 0, else 5m); the cache is warm until the time of the last request that wrote or read it plus that tier. The SDK screen gets usage on its result and assistant messages; for CLI panes, the session's transcript lines carry the same fields (the usage sweep already reads them).

Where:
- The Claude screen's status line, beside the context meter: 'warm 42m' in green, turning yellow under 5 minutes, 'cold' in plain once expired. It counts down live (once a minute is enough; once a second only in the last minute), with no timer running while the page is hidden.
- Each worker pane's row in the workers popup (Alt+W) shows its own warm or cold.
- Keep it to these two places; no new manager strip unless the user asks.

The rule (tier from usage, expiry from last use, the tone thresholds) is a small module with a test (workflow-rule-2). Help blurb stays under BLURB_WORD_LIMIT; detail in docs/chat README. No version bump (workflow-rule-3).

comments.body: Shipped in PR #189: warm/cold prompt cache pill on the Claude screen's status line (counts down, stops off view) and per-worker warm/cold in the workers popup; rule in src/shared/usage/cache-warmth.ts with tests; TTL facts cited in chat-decision-12. Hand check in the app not done.
